claim_level_review.scope: Three coordinator-authored claims and one rejected overgeneralization over the live source passages; no live reader answers were generated.

evidence.quote: proposes to use executable Python code to consolidate LLM agents’ actions into a unified action space (CodeAct).
generates fewer text tokens than the final agent in TextMAS across different model scales and tasks, with an average reduction of 29.1%.

claims.claim: CodeAct proposes executable Python as a unified agent action representation.
claims.rationale: The inspected abstract explicitly proposes this representation; it does not demonstrate a benefit for this repository.

claims.claim: The C2C setup includes OpenBookQA, MMLU-Redux, ARC-Challenge and C-Eval; the paper also reports LongBenchV1 experiments.
claims.rationale: Setup and appendix passages identify these benchmarks. The four setup names are not an exhaustive list of all evaluations.

claims.claim: LatentMAS authors report a 29.1% average reduction in final-answering-agent text tokens versus TextMAS under their reported settings.
claims.rationale: The inspected section explicitly excludes intermediate agents and compares final decoding stages; no result for this project follows.

claims.claim: The cited 29.1% establishes a 29.1% reduction in whole-system token usage or API cost.
claims.rationale: This statistic covers final-agent output text only. It does not measure total system tokens, latent computation, provider pricing, or this implementation.

claim_level_review.limitation: Small unblinded agent judgment, potentially fallible; not independent human review, a benchmark score, or proof of model improvement.
